questions.q: A particle is thrown with a speed $v$ from a point $O$ at an angle $\theta$ with the horizontal plane such that it passes through the point $P$ at a height of $1$ m and horizontal distance of $5$ m from $O$, as shown in the figure. If acceleration due to gravity is $g$ ms$^{-2}$, then the correct statement(s) is/are:
options: If $\theta = 45^\circ$, the particle reaches its maximum height before it reaches $P$.
If $\theta = 30^\circ$, the particle reaches its maximum height after reaching $P$.
questions.solution:
The equation of trajectory of a projectile is given by:

$y = x \tan \theta - \dfrac{g x^2}{2 v^2 \cos^2 \theta}$

The particle passes through point $P(5, 1)$. Substituting $x = 5$ and $y = 1$:

$1 = 5 \tan \theta - \dfrac{25 g}{2 v^2 \cos^2 \theta}$

For option (A), substituting $\theta = 45^\circ$:

$1 = 5 \tan 45^\circ - \dfrac{25 g}{2 v^2 \cos^2 45^\circ}$

$1 = 5(1) - \dfrac{25 g}{2 v^2 (1/2)}$

$1 = 5 - \dfrac{25 g}{v^2}$

$\dfrac{25 g}{v^2} = 4 \Rightarrow v^2 = \dfrac{25 g}{4} \Rightarrow v = \dfrac{5\sqrt{g}}{2}$ ms$^{-1}$

Thus, option (A) is correct.

For option (B), the horizontal distance to the maximum height is $x_m = \dfrac{R}{2} = \dfrac{v^2 \sin(2\theta)}{2g}$.

For $\theta = 45^\circ$ and $v^2 = \dfrac{25g}{4}$:

$x_m = \dfrac{\left(\dfrac{25g}{4}\right) \sin 90^\circ}{2g} = \dfrac{25}{8} = 3.125$ m

Since $x_m = 3.125$ m $< 5$ m, the particle reaches its maximum height before it reaches $P$. Thus, option (B) is correct.

For option (C), substituting $\theta = 30^\circ$ into the trajectory equation:

$1 = 5 \tan 30^\circ - \dfrac{25 g}{2 v^2 \cos^2 30^\circ}$

$1 = \dfrac{5}{\sqrt{3}} - \dfrac{25 g}{2 v^2 (3/4)} \Rightarrow \dfrac{50 g}{3 v^2} = \dfrac{5}{\sqrt{3}} - 1$

$v^2 = \dfrac{50\sqrt{3}g}{3(5 - \sqrt{3})}$

The horizontal distance to the maximum height is:

$x_m = \dfrac{v^2 \sin 60^\circ}{2g} = \dfrac{v^2 \sqrt{3}}{4g} = \dfrac{50\sqrt{3}g}{3(5 - \sqrt{3})} \times \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{4g} = \dfrac{25}{2(5 - \sqrt{3})} \approx 3.82$ m

Since $x_m < 5$ m, the particle reaches its maximum height before reaching $P$. Thus, option (C) is incorrect.

For option (D), substituting $\theta = \tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{1}{5}\right)$, so $\tan \theta = \dfrac{1}{5}$:

$1 = 5\left(\dfrac{1}{5}\right) - \dfrac{25 g}{2 v^2 \cos^2 \theta} \Rightarrow 1 = 1 - \dfrac{25 g}{2 v^2 \cos^2 \theta}$

$\dfrac{25 g}{2 v^2 \cos^2 \theta} = 0$

This is only possible if $v \to \infty$. Thus, option (D) is incorrect.

Answer: If $\theta = 45^\circ$, then $v = \dfrac{5\sqrt{g}}{2}$ ms$^{-1}$.; If $\theta = 45^\circ$, the particle reaches its maximum height before it reaches $P$.

questions.q: A projectile of mass 200 g is launched in a viscous medium at an angle $60^{\circ}$ with the horizontal, with an initial velocity of $270 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}$. It experiences a viscous drag force $\vec{F}=-c \vec{v}$ where the drag coefficient $c=0.1 \mathrm{~kg} / \mathrm{s}$ and $\vec{v}$ is the instantaneous velocity of the projectile. The projectile hits a vertical wall after 2 s . Taking $e=2.7$, the horizontal distance of the wall from the point of projection (in m ) is
questions.solution:
$\overrightarrow{\mathrm{F}_{\mathrm{net}}=\mathrm{m} \frac{\mathrm{ d} \overrightarrow{\mathrm{v}}}{\mathrm{dt}} \mathrm{mg}+\overrightarrow{\mathrm{F}}=\frac{\mathrm{md} \overrightarrow{\mathrm{v}}}{\mathrm{dt}} \mathrm{mg}-\mathrm{C} \overrightarrow{\mathrm{v}}=\frac{\mathrm{md} \overrightarrow{\mathrm{v}}}{\mathrm{dt}}$
Horizontal direction
$-\mathrm{Cv}_{\mathrm{x}}=\frac{\mathrm{mdv}_{\mathrm{x}}}{\mathrm{dt}} \begin{aligned} & -\frac{C}{m} \int_0^t d t=\int_{v_{0 x}}^{v_x} \frac{d v_x}{v_x} \\ & -\frac{t}{2}=\ell n \frac{v_x}{v_{0 x}} \\ & \frac{d x}{d t}=v_x=v_{0 x} e^{-t / 2} \\ & \int_0^{S_x} d x=v_{0 x} \int_0^t e^{-t / 2} d t \\ & S_x=2 v_{0 x}\left(1-e^{-t / 2}\right) \\ & \text{ at } t=2 \sec \end{aligned} \begin{aligned} & \mathrm{S}_{\mathrm{x}}=2 \times 270 \times \cos 60^{\circ}\left[1-\frac{1}{\mathrm{e}}\right] \\ & \mathrm{S}_{\mathrm{x}}=270\left(1-\frac{1}{2.7}\right) \\ & =\frac{270}{2.7} \times(1.7) \\ & =170 \mathrm{ m} \\ & \mathrm{ S}_{\mathrm{x}}=170 \mathrm{ m}\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A particle of mass $m$ is moving in the $xy$-plane such that its velocity at a point $( x, y )$ is given as $\overset{\to}{v} = \alpha\left(y\overset{∧}{x} + 2x\overset{∧}{y}\right)$ where $\alpha$ is a non-zero constant. What is the force $\overset{\to}{F}$ acting on the particle?
questions.solution:
As force is given by, $\overset{\to}{F} = m\dfrac{d\overset{\to}{v}}{dt}$.

Given: $\overset{\to}{v} = \alpha\left(y\overset{∧}{x} + 2x\overset{∧}{y}\right)$, where velocity along x-axis is ${v}_{x} = \alphay$ and velocity along y-axis is ${v}_{y} = 2x\alpha$.

Therefore,

$\dfrac{d\overset{\to}{v}}{dt} = \alpha\left(\dfrac{dy}{dt}\overset{∧}{x} + 2\dfrac{dx}{dt}\overset{∧}{y}\right)$

$= \alpha\left({v}_{y}\overset{∧}{x} + 2{v}_{x}\overset{∧}{y}\right)$

$= \alpha\left[2x\alpha\overset{∧}{x} + 2\alphay\overset{∧}{y}\right]$

$= 2{\alpha}^{2}\left[x\overset{∧}{x} + y\overset{∧}{y}\right]$

Therefore, required value of $\overset{\to}{F} = 2m{\alpha}^{2}\left[x\overset{∧}{x} + y\overset{∧}{y}\right]$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A slide with a frictionless curved surface, which becomes horizontal at its lower end, is fixed on the terrace of a building of height $3h$ from the ground, as shown in the figure. A spherical ball of mass $m$ is released on the slide from rest at a height $h$ from the top of the terrace. The ball leaves the slide with a velocity $\overset{\to}{u}0 = {u}_{0}\overset{∧}{x}$ and falls on the ground at a distance $d$ from the building making an angle $\theta$ with the horizontal. It bounces off with a velocity $\overset{\to}{v}$ and reaches a maximum height ${h}_{1}$. The acceleration due to gravity is $g$ and the coefficient of restitution of the ground is $\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}$. Which of the following statement(s) is(are) correct?
questions.solution:
Using energy conservation,

$mgh = \dfrac{1}{2}m{\left({u}_{0}\right)}^{2}$

$⇒ {u}_{0} = \sqrt{2gh}$

${u}_{0}$ is the horizontal component of the velocity throughout the flight. For vertical component of the velocity(just before collision with the ground), we can use equation of motion

${\left({v}_{z}\right)}^{2} = {0}^{2} + 2\left(- g\right)\left(- 3h\right) ⇒ {v}_{z} = \sqrt{6gh}$

Angle $\theta$ can be written as,

$tan\theta = \dfrac{{v}_{z}}{u} = \sqrt{3}$

$⇒ \theta = {60}^{o}$

Horizontal distance covered just before the collision will be,

$d = {u}_{0}T = {u}_{0}\sqrt{2\left(\dfrac{3h}{g}\right)} = \sqrt{2gh}\sqrt{\left(2\right)\left(\dfrac{3h}{g}\right)} = 2\sqrt{3}h$

After collision, only velocity along $z$-direction changes. Therefore,

${v}_{1} = e{v}_{z} = \sqrt{2gh}$ and hence

$\overset{\to}{v} = {u}_{0}\overset{∧}{i} + {v}_{1}\overset{∧}{k}$

$= \sqrt{2gh}\left[\overset{∧}{i} + \overset{∧}{k}\right] = \sqrt{2gh}\left[\overset{∧}{x} + \overset{∧}{z}\right]$

Now, maximum height achieved after collision will be,

${h}_{1} = \dfrac{{{v}_{1}}^{2}}{2g} = h$.

Finally, ${u}_{0} = \sqrt{2gh}, \theta = {60}^{o}, \dfrac{d}{{h}_{1}} = 2\sqrt{3}$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A person of height $1 . 6m$ is walking away from a lamp post of height $4m$ along a straight path on the flat ground. The lamp post and the person are always perpendicular to the ground. If the speed of the person is $60cm{s}^{- 1}$, the speed of the tip of the person’s shadow on the ground with respect to the person is _____ $cm{s}^{- 1}$.
questions.solution:
Given:

Speed of person $= \dfrac{d{x}_{1}}{dt} = 60cm{s}^{- 1}$

Also Speed of tip of person's shadow $= \dfrac{d{x}_{2}}{dt}$.

As $∆ ABE$ and $∆ DCE$ are similar triangles, therefore we can write

$\dfrac{4}{{x}_{2}} = \dfrac{1 . 6}{{x}_{2} - {x}_{1}}$

$⇒ 4{x}_{2} - 4{x}_{1} = 1 . 6{x}_{2}$

$⇒ 2 . 4{x}_{2} = 4{x}_{1}$

Differentiate both sides w.r.t. $t$, we get

$2 . 4\dfrac{d{x}_{2}}{dt} = 4\dfrac{d{x}_{1}}{dt}$

$⇒ \dfrac{d{x}_{2}}{dt} = \dfrac{4}{2 . 4}\left(60\right)$

$= 100cm{s}^{- 1}$

Now, speed of the tip of the person's shadow on the ground with respect to the person will be $\overset{\to}{v}SP = \overset{\to}{v}SG - \overset{\to}{v}PG$

$⇒ {v}_{SP} = 100cm{s}^{- 1} - 60cm{s}^{- 1}$

$= 40cm{s}^{- 1}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A projectile is fired from horizontal ground with speed $v$ and projection angle $\theta$. When the acceleration due to gravity is $g$, the range of the projectile is $d$. If at the highest point in its trajectory, the projectile enters a different region where the effective acceleration due to gravity is ${g}^{'} = \dfrac{g}{0 . 81}$, then the new range is ${d}^{'} = nd .$ The value of $n$ is
questions.solution:
Horizontal range of the projectile is $d = \dfrac{{v}^{2}sin2\theta}{g}$

Maximum height attained by the projectile is $H = \dfrac{{v}^{2}\sin^{2}\theta}{2g}$

So, after entering the new region, time taken by projectile to reach ground

$t = \sqrt{\dfrac{2H}{{g}^{'}}}$$= \sqrt{\dfrac{2\left(\dfrac{{v}^{2}\sin^{2}\theta}{2g}\right)}{\dfrac{g}{0 . 81}}}$

$= \dfrac{0 . 94vsin\theta}{g}$

So, horizontal displacement done by the projectile in new region is

$x = \dfrac{0 . 9vsin\theta}{g} \times vcos\theta$

$= 0 . 9\dfrac{{v}^{2}sin2\theta}{2g}$

So, new range is ${d}^{'} = \dfrac{d}{2} + x$

$= \dfrac{{v}^{2}sin2\theta}{2g} + 0 . 9\dfrac{{v}^{2}sin2\theta}{2g}$

$= 0 . 95d$

So, $n = 0 . 95d$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q:
A projectile is thrown from a point $\mathrm{O}$ on the ground at an angle $45^{\circ}$ from the vertical and with a speed $5 \sqrt{2} \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}$. The projectile at the highest point of its trajectory splits into two equal parts. One part falls vertically down to the ground, $0.5 \mathrm{~s}$ after the splitting. The other part, $t$ seconds after the splitting, falls to the ground at a distance $x$ meters from the point O. The acceleration due to gravity $g=10 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}^{2}$.
The value of $t$ is _________.
questions.solution:
After splitting of projectile in two equal parts one part falls vertically down to the ground.

So, velocity of another part will be according to conservation of linear momentum,

$m \times 5 = \dfrac{m}{2} \times 0 + \dfrac{m}{2} \times v$

$⇒ v = 10m{s}^{- 1}$

Now time taken by ${m}_{1}$, to reach ground,

since after splitting of projectile ${m}_{1}$ will perform horizontal projectile so,

$t = \sqrt{\dfrac{2h}{g}}$

$⇒ t = \sqrt{\dfrac{2{u}^{2}\sin^{2}\theta}{2{g}^{2}}}$

$⇒ t = \sqrt{\dfrac{2 \times 50}{2 \times 10 \times 10} \times \dfrac{1}{2}} = \sqrt{0.25}$

$⇒ t = 0.5s$

questions.q:
A projectile is thrown from a point $\mathrm{O}$ on the ground at an angle $45^{\circ}$ from the vertical and with a speed $5 \sqrt{2} \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}$. The projectile at the highest point of its trajectory splits into two equal parts. One part falls vertically down to the ground, $0.5 \mathrm{~s}$ after the splitting. The other part, $t$ seconds after the splitting, falls to the ground at a distance $x$ meters from the point O. The acceleration due to gravity $g=10 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}^{2}$.
The value of $x$ is ________.
questions.solution:
So,

$x = \dfrac{R}{2} + r$

Where,$R$ is the range of oblique projectile and $r$ is the range of horizontal projectile.

$x = \dfrac{R}{2} + 10 \times \sqrt{\dfrac{2h}{g}}$

$x = \dfrac{{u}^{2}sin2\theta}{g \times 2} + 10 \times 0.5$

$x = \dfrac{50}{20} + 5$

$x = 2.5 + 5$

questions.q: A ball is thrown from ground at an angle $\theta$ with horizontal and with an initial speed ${u}_{0} .$ For the resulting projectile motion, the magnitude of average velocity of the ball up to the point when it hits the ground for the first time is ${V}_{1} .$ After hitting the ground, ball rebounds at the same angle $\theta$ but with a reduced speed of $\dfrac{{u}_{0}}{\alpha} .$ Its motion continues for a long time as shown in figure. If the magnitude of average velocity of the ball for entire duration of motion is $0.8{V}_{1},$ the value of $\alpha$ is______
questions.solution:
For first projectile
Average velocity, $\left(V\right) = \dfrac{R}{T} = {U}_{x} = {V}_{1}\left(\begin{array}{ll}\left(whereR = RangeandT = Timeofflight\right) \\ R = \dfrac{2{U}_{x} . {U}_{y}}{g} T = \dfrac{2 . {U}_{y}}{g}\end{array}\right)$
For journey
${\left(V\right)}_{1 \to n} = \dfrac{{R}_{1} + {R}_{2} + \ldots + {R}_{n}}{{T}_{1} + {T}_{2} + \ldots + {T}_{n}} = \dfrac{\dfrac{2{u}_{{x}_{1}}{u}_{{y}_{1}}}{g} + \dfrac{2{u}_{{x}_{2}}{u}_{{y}_{2}}}{g} + \ldots + \dfrac{2{u}_{{x}_{n}}{u}_{{y}_{n}}}{g}}{\dfrac{2{u}_{{y}_{1}}}{g} + \dfrac{2{u}_{{y}_{2}}}{g} + \ldots \dfrac{2{u}_{{y}_{n}}}{g}}$
$⇒ {U}_{x}\left(\dfrac{1 + \dfrac{1}{{\alpha}^{2}} + \dfrac{1}{{\alpha}^{4}} + \ldots \dfrac{1}{{\alpha}^{2n}}}{1 + \dfrac{1}{\alpha} + \dfrac{1}{{\alpha}^{2}} + \ldots + \dfrac{1}{{\alpha}^{n}}}\right) = 0.8{v}_{1}, \left(\begin{array}{ll}1 + \dfrac{1}{{\alpha}^{2}} + \dfrac{1}{{\alpha}^{4}} + \ldots \dfrac{1}{{\alpha}^{2n}} ⇒ Geometricprogression \\ SumofG . P . = \dfrac{1}{1 - {\alpha}^{2}}\end{array}\right)$
$⇒ \dfrac{{V}_{1}\left(\dfrac{1}{1 - \dfrac{1}{{\alpha}^{2}}}\right)}{\left(\dfrac{1}{1 - \dfrac{1}{\alpha}}\right)} = 0.8{v}_{1} ⇒ \dfrac{\alpha}{1 + \alpha} = 0.8 ⇒ \alpha = 4$

questions.solution:
${H}_{1} = \dfrac{{u}^{2}\sin^{2} ⁡ {45}^{o}}{2g} = 120$

${H}_{2} = \dfrac{{\left(\dfrac{u}{\sqrt{2}}\right)}^{2}\sin^{2}30 °}{2g} = \dfrac{{u}^{2}}{16g} . . . \left(ii\right)$

${H}_{2} = \dfrac{{H}_{1}}{4} = 30m$

questions.q: Three vectors $\overset{\to}{P}, \overset{\to}{Q}$ and $\overset{\to}{R}$ are shown in the figure. Let, $S$ be any point on the vector $\overset{\to}{R}$ . The distance between the points $P$ and $S$ is $b\left|\overset{\to}{R}\right|$. The general relation among vectors $\overset{\to}{P}, \overset{\to}{Q}$ and $\overset{\to}{S}$ are
questions.solution:
Let, vector from point $P$ to point $S$ be $\overset{\to}{C}$, 

$⇒ \overset{\to}{C} = b\left|\overset{\to}{R}\right|\overset{^}{R} = b\left|\overset{\to}{R}\right|\left(\overset{\to}{R}\left|\overset{\to}{R}\right|\right) = b\overset{\to}{R} = b\left(\overset{\to}{Q} - \overset{\to}{P}\right)$

From triangle rule of vector addition, 

$\overset{\to}{P} + \overset{\to}{C} = \overset{\to}{S}$

$\overset{\to}{P} + b\left(\overset{\to}{Q} - \overset{\to}{P}\right) = \overset{\to}{S}$

$⇒ \overset{\to}{S} = \left(1 - b\right)\overset{\to}{P} + b\overset{\to}{Q}$

nearest integer \(=2 \mathrm{ s}\)$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A ball of mass $(m) 0.5 \mathrm{~kg}$ is attached to the end of a string having length $(L) 0.5 \mathrm{~m}$. The ball is rotated on a horizontal circular path about vertical axis. The maximum tension that the string can bear is $324 \mathrm{~N}$. The maximum possible value of angular velocity of ball (in rad/s) is
questions.solution:
$T \cos \theta$ component will cancel $\mathrm{mg}$.
$T \sin \theta$ component will provide necessary centripetal force to the ball towards centre $C$.
$ \begin{array}{rlrl} 
& \therefore & T \sin \theta & =m r \omega^2=m(l \sin \theta) \omega^2 \\
& \text{ or } & T & =m l \omega^2 \\
& \therefore & \omega & =\sqrt{\frac{T}{m l}} \\
& \text{ or } & \omega_{\max } & =\sqrt{\frac{T_{\max }}{m l}}=\sqrt{\frac{324}{0.5 \times 0.5}} \\
& = & 36 \mathrm{rad} / \mathrm{s}
\end{array}  \therefore$ Correct option is (d).
Analysis of Question
(i) Question is simple.
(ii) This is called the conical pendulum.
(iii) The interesting fact in this problem is that $\omega$ or $T$ is independent of $\theta$.
$\omega \propto \sqrt{T}$
If $\omega$ is increased, $T$ will also increase.

questions.question:
Statement 1 For an observer looking out through the window of a fast moving train, the nearby objects appear to move in the opposite direction to the train, while the distant objects appear to be stationary.
and Statement 2 If the observer and the object are moving at velocities $\overrightarrow{\mathbf{v}}_{\mathbf{1}}$ and $\overrightarrow{\mathbf{v}_2}$ respectively with reference to a laboratory frame, the velocity of the object with respect to the observer is $\overrightarrow{\mathbf{v}_2}-\overrightarrow{\mathbf{v}_1}$.
questions.explanation: Statement-2, is formula of relative velocity. But it does not explain statement-1 correctly. The correct explanation of statement-1 is due to visual perception of motion. The object appears to be moving faster, when its angular velocity is greater w.r.t observer. $\therefore$ correct answer is (b).
